claim_verdict: 94.56% SURVIVES as a server-reported instrument, WITH THREE STATED LIMITS (see findings). It must not be thrown out, but the paper must describe it as a provider-usage field, not as a measured cache-hit rate, and must use a MEDIAN-OVER-SESSIONS headline, not the sum ratio.
checks: cachedTokens is a pure pass-through of the provider usage object; no local estimate or derivation (findings[0])
inputTokens denominator comes from the same usage payload in the same settle call (dist/index.js:594; findings[1])
independent corroboration: 52,707 cacheLedger lines sum to input 3,804,227,263 / cached 3,597,266,905 = 94.5597%, matching stats_json (findings[2])
single self-hosted endpoint 127.0.0.1:8790, openai protocol, model deepseek-v4.1-flash; not a cloud-vendor or public-API result (findings[3])
LIMIT 1: cached semantics are protocol-dependent and stats_json stores no protocol flag (findings[4])
LIMIT 2: anthropic cache-write tokens are dropped from the denominator when input>=cached>0, which lowers the ratio (findings[5])
LIMIT 3: hitPct is integer-rounded but stored input/cached are raw, and the ratio was recomputed from raw integers (findings[6])
contamination not material: the 8 research sessions are 0.282% of input at 93.92%, so excluding them moves the rate +0.0018pp to 94.5615% (findings[10], findings[11], contamination.conclusion)
dispersion is the real fragility: 1130 of 1273 sessions carry cached>0, so the sum-ratio is not the typical session and median-over-sessions is the defensible headline (findings[12])
findings: `cachedTokens` is a PURE PASS-THROUGH of the provider `usage` object. There is no local estimate, heuristic, or derivation: the number is read straight out of the API usage payload and accumulated. It cannot be an estimate.

`inputTokens` (the denominator) is ALSO provider-reported, from the same `usage` object, and is accumulated in the same settle call as `cachedTokens` (dist/index.js:594 `stats.inputTokens+=s3.total`, immediately followed by `session.stats.cachedTokens+=s3.reportedCached`). Numerator and denominator therefore come from the SAME payload and are internally consistent.

A second, INDEPENDENT record of the same data corroborates it exactly: `sessions.metadata_json.cacheLedger.lines` holds one entry PER REQUEST (52707 lines across 1181 sessions), each carrying its own `input`/`cached`/`hitPct`/`model`/`proto`/`upstream`. Summing those per-request lines gives input=3,804,227,263 cached=3,597,266,905 rate=94.5597% — identical to the accumulated counters, to the token. The stats_json counter is not drifting from the underlying samples.

The provider here is a single self-hosted endpoint, http://127.0.0.1:8790 (all 1273 sessions: origin=8790, namespace='dsh'). The cached count is whatever THAT server reports in its usage object. The rate measures that server's KV-cache reuse, NOT a cloud vendor's prompt caching and not DeepSeek's public API. A paper must name the endpoint and the model id (deepseek-v4.1-flash appears in ledger lines).

LIMIT 1 — semantics are protocol-dependent and the DB stores no flag. `cachedTokens` means 'cache READ' and is EXCLUDED from input (additive), for anthropic. For openai/responses/google it means 'subset OF prompt_tokens' and is INCLUDED in input. The read code maps both: openai reads `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens ?? prompt_cache_hit_tokens`; anthropic reads `cache_read_input_tokens`; google reads `cachedContentTokenCount`. The denominator is repaired by `promptInputTotal` (dist/index.js:516) which adds cached back for split-semantics protocols. The flag is only present in cacheLedger lines (`proto`), not in stats_json.

LIMIT 2 — anthropic cache-WRITE tokens are DROPPED from the denominator. `promptInputTotal` only adds back `cached` and `creation` when `input < cached` (the split-semantics heuristic). On a partial page-cache miss where input>=cached>0, the additive branch is skipped and `cache_creation_input_tokens` is omitted. This is conservative (it lowers the ratio), so it does not inflate the claim.

LIMIT 3 — an arithmetic rounding, NOT a clamp. `hitPct` in log/ledger lines is `Math.round(cached/total*100)` (integer percent). The STORED stats_json and ledger `input`/`cached` fields are raw integers; I recomputed the ratio from raw integers, so this does not affect 94.56%. Note the display value hitPct is 0..100 and is not clamped at 100 in the accumulate path.

NON-DENOMINATOR compat bug found and excluded: an older buggy parse `num3(usage['input_tokens_details']['cached_tokens'])` (dist/index.js:885) reads the wrong (OpenAI-shaped) path for anthropic. It can only misrecord a cached count as undefined->null. Since it feeds the numerator only, on a hit it can only UNDERCOUNT cachedTokens. It cannot manufacture a high ratio, and for this DB all sessions are openai protocol.

`lastInputTokensSource` / `contextTokensSource` = 'usage' vs 'estimate' grade the CONTEXT/LAST-REQUEST size only (1059 usage vs 200 estimate; 1011 usage vs 262 estimate respectively). They do NOT grade `cachedTokens`. `lastInputTokensOrigin` and `calibratedEstimateOrigin` = 'http://127.0.0.1:8790' (an endpoint stamp, NOT a usage/estimate flag). `calibratedEstimate` is a dimensionless ratio (~0.9-1.4) used to calibrate the LOCAL estimate; it never touches cachedTokens. `localInputEstimate` is a separate local estimate and is NOT the denominator.

cacheSamples is a SAMPLE COUNTER, not a saturated guard: 55594 requests vs 55594 cacheSamples (1:1). Every request that reported usage produced a sample; there is no 'cachedTokens clamped to cacheSamples' behaviour.

CONTAMINATION — the research workspace is NOT absorbed by the DB. 8 sessions (1 root + 7 subagents) do belong to this research program: session-b61634cb-... (the parent research conversation, titles matching the caching experiment) and its forked subagent sessions. These 8 carry 10,729,113 input tokens, 10,076,928 cached tokens, 431 requests.

The exclusion does NOT move the headline: WITH research sessions 94.5597%; WITHOUT them 94.5615% (1265 sessions, 3,793,498,150 input, 3,587,189,977 cached). The research sessions alone sit at 93.92%, below the fleet average, so including them slightly LOWERS the number. The claim is not self-serving.

THE REAL FRAGILITY IS NOT CONTAMINATION, IT IS DISPERSION: because the sum-of-ratio is dominated by big sessions, the fleet number is not the typical session. Sessions with cachedTokens>0 = 1130 of 1273. A per-session median is the defensible headline; report both sum-ratio and median, and say which is which.
